title: Jonah and the Compass
premise: In the port city of Saltmere, Paloma Vane has survived five years of indenture to the Meridian Trading Company by making herself unremarkable—until a census taker's probing questions expose that her late mother was not merely a pearl diver but the illegitimate daughter of the company's founder. The discovery makes Paloma heir to a contested fortune and a target for the founder's legitimate descendants, who will burn the pearl workshop and everyone in it to bury the bloodline. As she races to finish her indenture and claim her inheritance before the workshop is 'closed for restructuring,' Paloma must choose between the safety of silence and an alliance with Elias, the census taker whose duty-bound honesty first endangered her. In the end, she trades the fortune itself for the freedom of the workshop's divers, exposing the family's corruption publicly and walking away with something rarer: a name she chose herself.
about_author: L. M. Delacroix is the pen name of a former maritime archivist who spent a decade cataloguing colonial trading ledgers along the Pearl Coast. Their novels excavate the lives history recorded only as line items.

chapters.title: The Weight of Water
chapters.summary: Paloma dives the morning beds, counting oysters by feel while the workshop overseer counts her. Her POV establishes the economy of silence she's built over five years of indenture. Emotional beat: quiet competence masking constant vigilance.

chapters.title: One Question Too Many
chapters.summary: Census taker Elias Corvane arrives to update the company rolls and asks for Paloma's mother's maiden name—a question no one has asked aloud in years. Paloma lies badly; he notices. His POV alternates, revealing his own orders to flag 'irregular bloodlines.' Beat: the first crack in her invisibility.

chapters.title: What Mother Kept
chapters.summary: Paloma searches her mother's sea chest and finds a locket containing a miniature portrait of old Augustin Meridian himself—and a half-burned letter naming her grandmother his daughter. Workshop matron Bess warns her to throw it into the tide. Beat: dread blooming where curiosity began.

chapters.title: The Founder's Ledger
chapters.summary: Elias cross-references census answers against company archives and finds a payment record: monthly sums to a diver named Sera Vane, annotated 'family obligation.' He sits on the finding, torn between duty and conscience. Beat: complicity begins.

chapters.title: Silvers and Salt
chapters.summary: Paloma and Elias meet again at the harbor market; their sparring turns unexpectedly honest over cheap coffee. She tests him with a false confidence; he doesn't report it. Beat: wary attraction, each recognizing the other's loneliness.

chapters.title: The Heir Who Visits
chapters.summary: Augustin's grandson, Aldous Meridian, tours the workshop with cold courtesy, asking Paloma oddly personal questions about her mother. That night, the workshop's records room is searched. Beat: the threat acquires a face.

chapters.title: Indenture Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Paloma calculates: eleven months remain on her contract. If she can hold out and prove descent before the workshop's lease expires, the inheritance clause in the founder's will activates. Bess reveals she helped hide Sera's papers years ago. Beat: hope with a deadline.

chapters.title: A Duty of Paper
chapters.summary: Elias is ordered to certify the workshop's census entries as 'complete'—a bureaucratic erasure that would legally dissolve any Vane claims. His POV shows the machinery of corruption working through ordinary forms. Beat: duty curdles into complicity.

chapters.title: The Diver's Oath
chapters.summary: Paloma confides in three trusted divers, who swear to help her recover the original will from the company house. One, Teo, is caught copying a key impression and punished brutally. Beat: guilt—the cost of involving others.

chapters.title: Storm Season
chapters.summary: A hurricane closes the beds; inside the barracks, Paloma and Elias, sheltering together, exchange truths—her lineage, his orders. Neither fully trusts, but they strike a bargain: he'll delay certification, she'll find proof. Beat: intimacy forged under pressure.

chapters.title: What the Tide Returned
chapters.summary: After the storm, the sea gives back a wreck—Augustin's private yacht, sunk decades ago. Among the salvage, divers find a sealed strongbox. Paloma realizes her mother may have hidden the true will aboard it long ago. Beat: fate offering a hand.

chapters.title: The Strongbox
chapters.summary: Opening the corroded box yields the will—and letters proving Aldous's father forged the original to disinherit Sera. But Aldous learns of the salvage and doubles his timeline: the workshop will be shuttered within weeks. Beat: triumph immediately shadowed.

chapters.title: Bargains in the Dark
chapters.summary: Aldous offers Paloma a quiet settlement: money, passage anywhere, silence forever. She pretends to consider while learning how much he knows—and that he suspects Elias. Beat: playing the game without becoming it.

chapters.title: The Turned Key
chapters.summary: Teo, broken by punishment, betrays the strongbox's location to Aldous's men. The will is stolen from its hiding place beneath the drying racks. Paloma's network scatters in fear. Beat: the floor drops out.

chapters.title: Ash and Ledger
chapters.summary: A fire guts the records annex; Elias realizes Aldous intends to destroy every document, then every witness. He copies what remains of the census archive into his memory and smuggles notes to Paloma. Beat: Elias finally chooses her over the institution.

chapters.title: Witnesses
chapters.summary: Paloma gathers testimony: Bess's memory of Sera, the payment ledgers Elias memorized, the divers' accounts of Aldous's enforcers. They plan to present everything at the magistrate's quarterly sitting—in nine days, one day after the workshop closes. Beat: resolve hardening into strategy.

chapters.title: Nine Days
chapters.summary: A countdown chapter: sabotage, bribed guards, a near-miss arrest. Paloma finishes her final required dive for the company, surfacing with the last pearls she'll ever owe them. Beat: endurance as defiance.

chapters.title: The Closing of the Workshop
chapters.summary: Aldous seals the gates and dismisses the divers onto the street. Paloma walks out last, carrying nothing visible—but Bess slips her the recovered half-letter, lifted from the fire wreckage. Beat: grief transmuted into purpose.

chapters.title: The Magistrate's Sitting
chapters.summary: Paloma presents her case: the will's terms recited from Elias's memory, witnesses, the forged signature pattern. Aldous produces the stolen 'original.' Then the salvaged strongbox's seal—unbroken, dated—is produced, proving his copy fake. Beat: climax; truth against power.

chapters.title: Verdict
chapters.summary: The magistrate voids the forged succession and recognizes Paloma's claim. Aldous, facing fraud charges, offers everything to make it go away. Paloma names her price: not the fortune, but the workshop's charter transferred to a divers' cooperative, and full pardons for her helpers. Beat: power refused and redirected.

chapters.title: A Name Chosen
chapters.summary: Paloma signs the cooperative charter as 'Paloma Vane'—the name her mother gave her, now hers by choice rather than survival. She and Elias, both freed from their institutions, stand awkwardly at the harbor deciding what comes next. Beat: tenderness after ordeal.

chapters.title: Jonah and the Compass
chapters.summary: Epilogue, one year later. The workshop thrives under the cooperative; Paloma teaches children to read the water. A compass her mother once owned hangs above the door, its needle pointing not north but toward the open sea. Final beat: inheritance redefined—not what we're given, but what we give forward.
